Armstrong was born in rural [Washington Township](/wiki/Washington_Township,_Auglaize_County,_Ohio "Washington Township, Auglaize County, Ohio"), in [Auglaize County, Ohio](/wiki/Auglaize_County,_Ohio "Auglaize County, Ohio"),[[5]](#cite_note-5) on August 5, 1930, the son of Viola Louise (née Engel) and Stephen Koenig Armstrong. He was of German, English, Scots-Irish, Irish, and Scottish descent.[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200513,_20-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) He is a descendant of [Clan Armstrong](/wiki/Clan_Armstrong "Clan Armstrong").[[9]](#cite_note-9) He had a younger sister, June, and a younger brother, Dean. His father was an [auditor](/wiki/Auditor "Auditor") for the [Ohio state government](/wiki/Government_of_Ohio "Government of Ohio"),[[10]](#cite_note-10) and the family moved around the state repeatedly, living in 16 towns over the next 14 years.[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200529-11) Armstrong's love for flying grew during this time, having started at the age of two when his father took him to the [Cleveland Air Races](/wiki/National_Air_Races "National Air Races"). When he was five or six, he experienced his first airplane flight in [Warren, Ohio](/wiki/Warren,_Ohio "Warren, Ohio"), when he and his father took a ride in a [Ford Trimotor](/wiki/Ford_Trimotor "Ford Trimotor") (also known as the "Tin Goose").[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200545-13) Armstrong constructed and flew model aircraft, beginning in his youth.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

The family's last move was in 1944 and took them back to Wapakoneta, where Armstrong attended [Blume High School](/wiki/Blume_High_School "Blume High School") and took flying lessons at the Wapakoneta airfield.[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHansen200549–50-15) He earned a student flight certificate on his 16th birthday, then [soloed](/wiki/First_solo_flight "First solo flight") in August, all before he had a driver's license.[[

Australia :: Demographics :: Health :: chunk_0031
See also: [Health care in Australia](/wiki/Health_care_in_Australia "Health care in Australia")

Australia's life expectancy of 83 years (81 years for males and 85 years for females)[[325]](#cite_note-336) is the [fifth-highest in the world](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy "List of countries by life expectancy"). It has the highest rate of skin cancer in the world,[[326]](#cite_note-337) while [cigarette smoking](/wiki/Tobacco_smoking "Tobacco smoking") is the largest preventable cause of death and disease, responsible for 7.8% of the total mortality and disease. Ranked second in preventable causes is [hypertension](/wiki/Hypertension "Hypertension") at 7.6%, with obesity third at 7.5%.[[327]](#cite_note-338)[[328]](#cite_note-339) Australia ranked 35th in the world in 2012 for its proportion of obese women[[329]](#cite_note-340) and near the top of [developed nations](/wiki/Developed_country "Developed country") for its proportion of [obese](/wiki/Obesity_in_Australia "Obesity in Australia") adults;[[330]](#cite_note-341) 63% of its adult population is either overweight or obese.[[331]](#cite_note-342)

Australia spent about 9.91% of its total GDP to health care in 2021.[[332]](#cite_note-343) It introduced a [national insurance scheme](/wiki/National_health_insurance "National health insurance") in 1975.[[333]](#cite_note-Biggs-2004-344) Following a period in which access to the scheme was restricted, the scheme became [universal](/wiki/Universal_health_care "Universal health care") once more in 1981 under the name of [Medicare](/wiki/Medicare_(Australia) "Medicare (Australia)").[[334]](#cite_note-345) The program is nominally funded by an income tax surcharge known as the [Medicare levy](/wiki/Medicare_levy "Medicare levy"), currently at 2%.[[335]](#cite_note-346) The states manage hospitals and attached outpatient services, while the Commonwealth funds the [Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme](/wiki/Pharmac

fanoutqa_032147.t: Salem, Oregon :: Parks and recreation :: Recreation :: chunk_0022
fanoutqa_032147.x:
Salem, Oregon :: Parks and recreation :: Recreation :: chunk_0022
Other large parks located in the Salem area include the 1,680-acre (680 ha) Willamette Mission State Park north of the city, and Silver Falls State Park east of Salem. Both of these parks have extensive hiking, biking, and horse trails.

Salem's central location provides access to a wide variety of recreational activities in a variety of climates and geographies year round. The [Coast Range](/wiki/Oregon_Coast_Range "Oregon Coast Range") and the Pacific Ocean are to the west. The Santiam Canyon area, the [Western Cascades](/wiki/Western_Cascades "Western Cascades") and the [High Cascades](/wiki/Cascade_Range "Cascade Range") are to the east. Portland and its environs are to the north, while Eugene and its environs are to the south.

Salem also has two disc golf courses. A nine-hole course located in the woods of Woodmansee Park (located behind Judson Middle School), and a more open style 18-hole course located throughout Cascade Gateway Park. They are both free and open to the public.

**Pittsburgh** ([/ˈpɪtsbɜːrɡ/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [*PITS-burg*](/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")) is a city in [Allegheny County, Pennsylvania](/wiki/Allegheny_County,_Pennsylvania "Allegheny County, Pennsylvania"), United States, and its [county seat](/wiki/County_seat "County seat"). Located in [southwestern Pennsylvania](/wiki/Western_Pennsylvania "Western Pennsylvania") where the [Allegheny](/wiki/Allegheny_River "Allegheny River") and [Monongahela](/wiki/Monongahela_River "Monongahela River") Rivers meet to form the [Ohio River](/wiki/Ohio_River "Ohio River"), it had a population of 302,971 at the 2020 census, making it the [second-most populous city](/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Pennsylvania#Municipalities "List of municipalities in Pennsylvania") in Pennsylvania after [Philadelphia](/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"). The [Pittsburgh metropolitan area](/wiki/Greater_Pittsburgh "Greater Pittsburgh") has over 2.43 million people, making it the largest in the Ohio Valley and [Appalachia](/wiki/Appalachia "Appalachia"), the [second-largest in Pennsylvania](/wiki/Pennsylvania_metropolitan_areas "Pennsylvania metropolitan areas"), and the [28th-largest in the U.S.](/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_statistical_areas "List of metropolitan statistical areas") The greater [Pittsburgh–Weirton–Steubenville combined statistical area](/wiki/Pittsburgh%E2%80%93New_Castle%E2%80%93Weirton_combined_statistical_area "Pittsburgh–New Castle–Weirton combined statistical area") includes parts of [Ohio](/wiki/Ohio "Ohio") and [West Virginia](/wiki/West_Virginia "West Virginia").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Polkcabinet1849edited.png/250px-Polkcabinet1849edited.png)](/wiki/File:Polkcabinet1849edited.png)

Buchanan (second from the left) in Polk's cabinet, 1849

Buchanan was offered the position of [Secretary of State](/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State") in the Polk administration or a seat on the [Supreme Court](/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") in recognition of his support in the election campaign. He accepted the State Department post and served for the duration of Polk's single term in office. During his tenure, the United States recorded its largest territorial expansion through the [Oregon Treaty](/wiki/Oregon_Treaty "Oregon Treaty") and the [Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo](/wiki/Treaty_of_Guadalupe_Hidalgo "Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo").[[33]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaker200438–40-33) In negotiations with Britain over Oregon, Buchanan initially favored the [49th parallel](/wiki/49th_parallel_north "49th parallel north") as the boundary of Oregon Territory, while Polk called for a more northerly boundary line. He later adopted a more expansionist position aligned with [Fifty-Four Forty or Fight](/wiki/Fifty-Four_Forty_or_Fight "Fifty-Four Forty or Fight"), before ultimately supporting the Oregon Compromise of 1846, which established the 49th parallel as the boundary in the [Pacific Northwest](/wiki/Pacific_Northwest "Pacific Northwest").[[34]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaker200440–41-34)

Buchanan believed that Mexico's April 1846 attack on American troops on the other side of the [Rio Grande](/wiki/Rio_Grande "Rio Grande") constituted a border violation and a legitimate reason for war. He was a member of the legendary [FC Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") team, coached by [Jack Greenwell](/wiki/Jack_Greenwell "Jack Greenwell"), that, apart from Sagibarba, also included [Paulino Alcántara](/wiki/Paulino_Alc%C3%A1ntara "Paulino Alcántara"), [Ricardo Zamora](/wiki/Ricardo_Zamora "Ricardo Zamora"), [Félix Sesúmaga](/wiki/F%C3%A9lix_Ses%C3%BAmaga "Félix Sesúmaga") and, later, [Franz Platko](/wiki/Franz_Platko "Franz Platko"). Between 1919 and 1933 he won twelve [Campionat de Catalunya](/wiki/Catalan_football_championship "Catalan football championship") titles, five [Copa del Rey](/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") and the very first [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") title in the [1929 season](/wiki/La_Liga_1929 "La Liga 1929"). Among the goals he scored were four in the [Copa del Rey](/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") finals of 1922, 1925, 1926 and 1928.

Genetic studies indicate that the Alaskan Husky originates from pre-Colonial North American Arctic village dogs (including precursors to the Alaskan Malamute) and Siberian imports (precursors to the Siberian Husky), crossbred with European breeds such as [Pointers](/wiki/Pointer_(dog_breed) "Pointer (dog breed)"), [German Shepherd Dogs](/wiki/German_Shepherd_Dogs "German Shepherd Dogs"), and [Salukis](/wiki/Saluki "Saluki") to improve its performance.[[9]](#cite_note-:1-9)[[8]](#cite_note-:6-8)

In 2015, a [DNA](/wiki/DNA "DNA") study indicated that the Alaskan husky, the [Siberian Husky](/wiki/Siberian_Husky "Siberian Husky"), and the [Alaskan Malamute](/wiki/Alaskan_Malamute "Alaskan Malamute") share a close genetic relationship between each other and were related to [Chukotka sled-dogs](/wiki/Chukotka_sled_dog "Chukotka sled dog") from [Siberia](/wiki/Siberia "Siberia"). They were separate from the two [Inuit dogs](/wiki/Canadian_Eskimo_Dog "Canadian Eskimo Dog"): the [Canadian Eskimo Dog](/wiki/Canadian_Eskimo_Dog "Canadian Eskimo Dog") and the [Greenland Dog](/wiki/Greenland_Dog "Greenland Dog"). The Siberian Husky and the Malamute both had maintained their Siberian lineage and had contributed significantly to the Alaskan husky, which was developed through crossing with [European](/wiki/Europe "Europe") breeds.[[8]](#cite_note-:6-8)

Other breeds identified as having contributed to the Alaskan husky sled dog gene pool include Pointers, and a number of other non-arctic breeds by breed and type group. The film received universal critical acclaim. The website's critical consensus reads, "An achingly sad anti-war film, *Grave of the Fireflies* is one of Studio Ghibli's most profoundly beautiful, haunting works."[[75]](#cite_note-:6-78) [Metacritic](/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") assigned the film a score of 94 out of 100 based on 16 reviews, indicating "universal acclaim".[[76]](#cite_note-79)

[Roger Ebert](/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of the *[Chicago Sun-Times](/wiki/Chicago_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")* considered it to be one of the best and most powerful war films ever made, and included it on his list of great films in 2000.[[60]](#cite_note-ebert-63)

Japanese filmmaker [Akira Kurosawa](/wiki/Akira_Kurosawa "Akira Kurosawa") praised the film and considered it his favourite Studio Ghibli production. He wrote a letter of praise to the studio's founder [Hayao Miyazaki](/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki "Hayao Miyazaki"), mistakenly believing he had directed it. Miyazaki himself praised the film as Takahata's masterpiece, but criticized the character of Seita for not behaving how he believed the son of a navy lieutenant should have behaved.[[77]](#cite_note-80)

On February 21, 2022, it was reported that Spears signed a $15 million book deal for her then-upcoming memoir, one of the [biggest book deals of all time](/wiki/List_of_largest_book_deals "List of largest book deals"),[[3]](#cite_note-biggest_book_deal-3) three months after a Los Angeles Superior Court Judge formally ended her [conservatorship](/wiki/Britney_Spears_conservatorship_case "Britney Spears conservatorship case").[[4]](#cite_note-4) On July 11, 2023, Spears announced that the book would be titled *The Woman in Me*, and would be released on October 24, 2023.[[5]](#cite_note-5) The title is a reference to a lyric in her song "[I'm Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman](/wiki/I%27m_Not_a_Girl,_Not_Yet_a_Woman "I'm Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman")" (2001), where she sings "I'm just trying to find the woman in me".[[6]](#cite_note-6) It was reportedly [ghostwritten](/wiki/Ghostwriter "Ghostwriter") together with journalist [Sam Lansky](/wiki/Sam_Lansky "Sam Lansky").[[7]](#cite_note-:1-7)

The book contains 288 pages comprising 49 chapters, and was released in 26 languages.[[8]](#cite_note-:3-8)[[9]](#cite_note-:4-9) The memoir was released in audiobook format simultaneously with the other editions.[[10]](#cite_note-:2-10) Spears confirmed she would not fully narrate the audiobook due to its "heart-wrenching and emotional" content, enlisting actress [Michelle Williams](/wiki/Michelle_Williams_(actress) "Michelle Williams (actress)") to record the main bulk of the audiobook, while Spears would participate by reading its introduction.[[10]](#cite_note-:2-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11) She promoted the memoir in *[People](/wiki/People_(magazine) "People (magazine)")* by providing insights into its content, accompanied by a cover photoshoot, which she had not done since 2016.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

Official languages in South America

Spanish and [Portuguese](/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") are the most spoken languages in South America, with approximately 200 million speakers each. Spanish is the official language of most countries, along with other native languages in some countries. Portuguese is the official language of Brazil.[[r]](#cite_note-227) [Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language") is the official language of [Suriname](/wiki/Suriname "Suriname"); English is the official language of [Guyana](/wiki/Guyana "Guyana"), although there are at least twelve other languages spoken in the country, including [Portuguese](/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"), Chinese, [Hindustani](/wiki/Caribbean_Hindustani "Caribbean Hindustani") and several native languages.[[210]](#cite_note-228) English is also spoken in the [Falkland Islands](/wiki/Falkland_Islands "Falkland Islands"). French is the official language of [French Guiana](/wiki/French_Guiana "French Guiana") and the second language in [Amapá](/wiki/Amap%C3%A1 "Amapá"), Brazil.

When subsequent planets were discovered in the 18th and 19th centuries, Uranus was named for a [Greek deity](/wiki/Uranus_(mythology) "Uranus (mythology)") and Neptune for a [Roman one](/wiki/Neptune_(mythology) "Neptune (mythology)") (the counterpart of [Poseidon](/wiki/Poseidon "Poseidon")). The asteroids were initially named from mythology as well—[Ceres](/wiki/Ceres_(mythology) "Ceres (mythology)"), [Juno](/wiki/Juno_(mythology) "Juno (mythology)"), and [Vesta](/wiki/Vesta_(mythology) "Vesta (mythology)") are major Roman goddesses, and Pallas is an epithet of the major Greek goddess [Athena](/wiki/Athena_(mythology) "Athena (mythology)")—but as more and more were discovered, they first started being named after more minor goddesses, and the mythological restriction was dropped starting from the twentieth asteroid [Massalia](/wiki/20_Massalia "20 Massalia") in 1852.[[245]](#cite_note-248) Pluto was named after the [Greek god of the underworld](/wiki/Pluto_(mythology) "Pluto (mythology)")), who could make himself invisible, since the search for [Planet X](/wiki/Planet_X "Planet X") had taken so long. (And secondarily because the first two letters are [Percival Lowell](/wiki/Percival_Lowell "Percival Lowell")'s initials.)[[246]](#cite_note-249)

The names of Uranus ([天](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%A4%A9 "wikt:天")王星 "sky king star"), Neptune ([海](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E6%B5%B7 "wikt:海")王星 "sea king star"), and Pluto ([冥](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E5%86%A5 "wikt:冥")王星 "underworld king star") in Chinese, Korean, and Japanese are [calques](/wiki/Calque "Calque") based on the roles of those gods in Roman and Greek mythology.[[247]](#cite_note-bianyulin-250)[[248]](#cite_note-251)[[d]](#cite_note-253) In the 19th century, [Alexander Wylie](/wiki/Alexander_Wylie_(missionary) "Alexander Wylie (missionary)") and [Li Shanlan](/wiki/Li_Shanlan "Li Shanlan") calqued the names of the first
